## Overview

This vignette describes how to calibrate an
[Atlantis](https://research.csiro.au/atlantis/) ecosystem model with the
**[calibrar](https://github.com/roliveros-ramos/calibrar)** package.  The example
uses the South East Australia Atlantis model (SETAS) and is designed to run on
a multi-core server or HPC cluster.

The calibration estimates **multiplicative factors** for selected biological
and fishing parameters of the model.  For each parameter and group, calibrar
proposes a value `p` in log scale; the model is run with the original value of
the parameter multiplied by `exp(p)`, so `p = 0` is the original model.
Each model run is compared with **targets** (biomass, weight at age,
abundance at age and catch), and the AHR-ES evolutionary algorithm searches for
the factors that best fit all the targets.

The workflow has six steps:

1. Prepare the model configuration and the input files.
2. Choose the parameters to calibrate for each functional group.
3. Create the calibration targets, settings and parameters.
4. Read the calibration inputs and build the objective function.
5. Run the calibration in parallel.
6. Inspect the results.

## 1. Model configuration and input files

The package uses the following folder structure (all paths are relative to the
project root, found with `here::here()`):

```
inputs/                       # files created for the calibration
  data/                       # target time series, one CSV per target
  parameter_table.csv         # parameters to calibrate for each group (step 2)
  reproduction-option.csv     # recruitment option of each group (step 2)
  model_configuration/        # all the files needed to run the model
    outputFolder/             # outputs of a previous run of the model
outputs/                      # plots
  keep_track_calibration/     # parameter files used in each run of each iteration
```

`inputs/model_configuration` contains the Atlantis model files: functional
groups, biology, harvest and run parameter files, initial conditions, forcing,
the shell script that runs the model (the only file with extension `.sh`),
and the observed time series used as targets.

```{r model-files}
fg.file     <- "SETasGroupsDem.csv"                 # functional groups
biology.prm <- "VMPA_setas_biol_fishing_Trunk.prm"  # biology parameters
run.prm     <- "VMPA_setas_run_fishing_F_Trunk.prm" # run parameters (tstop)
init.file   <- "INIT_VMPA_Jan2015.nc"               # initial conditions
biom.indx   <- "outputSETASBiomIndx.txt"            # biomass index of a previous run, in outputFolder
catch.file  <- "catch_timeseries.csv"               # observed catch: Code, Year, Catch
```

### Requirements for the model configuration

* **Functional groups file.**  Add a column `IsCalibrated`, set to `1` for the
  groups that are calibrated and `0` for those that are not.  Only groups with
  `IsTurnedOn == 1` and `IsCalibrated == 1` are calibrated.
* **Shell script.**  The shell script that runs Atlantis is found by its
  extension: there must be exactly one `.sh` file in the model directory.
  The biology and harvest parameter files are the ones given to its options
  `-b` and `-h`.  At every run, `run_model()` writes the edited parameters to
  these same files, so the shell script does not need to be changed.  The
  first time it runs in a directory, it keeps a copy of each original file as
  `<file>.original`, and the factors are always applied to the values in this
  copy.  `read_sh_file()` shows the files used by the shell script:

  ```{r read-sh}
  read_sh_file(here::here("inputs", "model_configuration"))
  ```

* **Output time steps.**  The model outputs are compared with the last
  `dt.timeseries` output time steps of each run, so the run length (`tstop`)
  and output frequency (`toutinc`) in the run parameter file must be set so
  that the last `dt.timeseries` outputs correspond to the period of the
  targets.  A run is considered crashed if it stops before `tstop`; all its
  outputs are then set to zero.

## 2. Choose the parameters to calibrate

The parameters to calibrate, and the groups each one applies to, are set in
`inputs/parameter_table.csv`.  It has one row per functional group (column
`Code`) and one column per parameter, set to `1` if the parameter is calibrated
for that group and `0` if not.  The optional columns `GroupType`,
`IsTurnedOn` and `IsCalibrated` are also used if present.

| Column | Parameter | Edited in |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| `mum` | Maximum growth rate | biology `.prm` |
| `BHalpha`, `BHbeta` | Beverton-Holt recruitment | biology `.prm` |
| `KDENR` | Recruits per adult | biology `.prm` |
| `mfc` | Fishing mortality (`mFC`) | harvest `.prm` |
| `mQ`, `mL` | Quadratic and linear mortality | biology `.prm` |
| `C` | Clearance rate | biology `.prm` |
| `E` | Assimilation efficiency | biology `.prm` |

It is best to calibrate one parameter per sensitive process.  Some rules are
applied on top of the table:

* `BHalpha`, `BHbeta` and `KDENR` are only calibrated for vertebrates
  (`GroupType` `FISH`, `SHARK`, `BIRD` or `MAMMAL`).
* `KDENR` is only calibrated for groups with recruitment option
  `flagrecruit = 12`, and `BHalpha` and `BHbeta` for groups with
  `flagrecruit = 3` (Beverton-Holt).
* `mfc` is only calibrated for groups with `IsFished == 1`.

The recruitment option of each group is read from the biology parameter file
with `repro_option()`, which writes `inputs/reproduction-option.csv`:

```{r repro-option}
atlantiscalibration::repro_option(fg.file, biology.prm)

parameter.file <- "parameter_table.csv"
atlantiscalibration::read_parameter_table(parameter.file)
```

## 3. Create the calibration targets, settings and parameters

`make_calsettings()` creates all the files needed for the calibration:

* **Targets**, one CSV per target in `inputs/data`:

  | `var.type` | Target | Source | Likelihood |
  |------------|--------|--------|------------|
  | `"biomass"` | `<Code>_biomass` | Initial biomass, from the biomass index of a previous run | `fun.type` |
  | `"weight"` | `<Name><age>_w` | Initial weight at age, from the initial conditions | `fun.type` |
  | `"abundance"` | `<Name>_Nums` | Initial abundance at age, from the initial conditions | `multinom` |
  | `"catch"` | `<Name>_catch` | Median observed catch | `fun.type` |

  Each target is constant over `dt.timeseries` time steps.  Biomass targets
  can also be created from an observed biomass time series (see
  `create_target_files_biomass()`, `time.series = TRUE`).
* **`inputs/calibration_settings_*.csv`**: one CSV file per target type
  (e.g., `calibration_settings_biomass.csv`, `calibration_settings_abundance.csv`),
  with one row per target in that type. Each row contains the
  likelihood (`type`), weight, data file and column (`varid`).  Use `w.vector`
  to give different weights to some groups.
* **`inputs/calibration-parameters-complete.csv`**: one row per factor to
  estimate, named after the parameter and group (e.g. `mum_FPS_factor`,
  `ZS_mQ_factor`), with its initial value (`paropt = 0`), bounds
  (`parmin = -1`, `parmax = 1`, i.e. factors between `exp(-1) = 0.37` and
  `exp(1) = 2.7`) and phase (`parphase`).  The bounds and phases can be edited
  in this file before step 4.

```{r make-calsettings}
var.type      <- c("biomass","abundance") #  "weight", "abundance", "catch" target types
fun.type      <- "lnorm2"  # likelihood for biomass, weight and catch targets
dt.timeseries <- 365        # number of time steps of each target in days, equivalent to tstop in the run file
w.vector      <- NULL      # different weights for some groups, e.g.
# w.vector <- tibble::tibble(Code = c("FPS", "FVS"), weight_new = c(0.5, 0.5))

atlantiscalibration::make_calsettings(fg.file = fg.file,
                 var.type       = var.type,
                 fun.type       = fun.type,
                 dt.timeseries  = dt.timeseries,
                 w.vector       = w.vector,
                 biology.prm    = biology.prm,
                 biom.indx      = biom.indx,
                 init.file      = init.file,
                 catch.file     = catch.file,
                 parameter.file = parameter.file)
```

`fun.type` can be any likelihood available in calibrar (see
`?calibrar::calibration_setup`) or a user-defined function.  The package
includes `likelihood_function()`, which penalises simulated values outside a
minimum-maximum envelope given by two columns of observed data; to use it, set
`type` to `likelihood_function` for those targets in any of the
`calibration_settings_*.csv` files.

## 4. Read the calibration inputs and build the objective function

`read_calibration()` reads the settings and targets with calibrar, reads the
parameters, builds the objective function and sets up the optimiser.  The
objective function runs the model with `run_model()`, which, at every
parameter proposal:

1. multiplies the original value of each calibrated parameter by its factor
   and writes it to the biology (`-b`) and harvest (`-h`) parameter files of
   the shell script,
2. runs Atlantis with the shell script,
3. reads the outputs and returns one element per target: biomass by group,
   weight at age, catch summed over fleets, and abundance at age.  If the run
   crashed, all outputs are zero.

The parameter files used in every model run are saved in
`outputs/keep_track_calibration` (argument `track.path`), with one folder per
iteration (generation) and the run number in the file name:

```
outputs/keep_track_calibration/
  iteration_001/
    run_001_calibration-parameters.csv        # factors of run 1
    run_001_VMPA_setas_biol_fishing_Trunk.prm # biology parameters of run 1
    run_001_VMPA_setas_harvest_F_Trunk.prm    # harvest parameters, if mfc is calibrated
    run_002_...
  iteration_002/
  ...
  final_001/                                  # best solution at the end of phase 1
    run_000_...
```

The run number is the calibrar run directory (`<run>/i1`, `<run>/i2`, ...).
The best solution is evaluated again in `<run>/i0` at the end of each phase,
and saved in `final_<phase>`.  The iteration is counted
in each run directory, so it continues correctly when a calibration is
restarted.

calibrar copies the `master` directory to a new directory under `run` for
each model run, so `master` must contain all the files needed to run the
model, and the arguments of `run_model()` are file names relative to it.

```{r read-calibration}
calibration <- atlantiscalibration::read_calibration(
  calibration.settings   = "calibration_settings_*.csv",
  calibration.parameters = "calibration-parameters-complete.csv",
  n.Cores      = 16,  # parallel workers and model runs per generation
  maxgen       = 3,   # maximum number of generations; increase for production
  master       = here::here("inputs","model_configuration"),
  run          = here::here("RUN"),
  restart.file = here::here("inputs","restart_file"),
  track.path   = here::here("outputs", "keep_track_calibration"), # parameter files of each run
  REPORT = 1,    # number of iterations to run before saving a restart
  parallel = TRUE, #run as parallel
  no.trace = 3, #global fitness and partial fitness
  # arguments of run_model(), relative to the master directory
  prefix        = "outputFolder/outputSETAS",            # -o outputSETAS.nc, -d outputFolder
  fg.file       = fg.file,
  biom.indx     = "outputFolder/outputSETASBiomIndx.txt", # written by each run
  run.prm       = run.prm,
  dt.timeseries = dt.timeseries
)
```

The control settings passed to calibrar are:

| Setting | Value | Purpose |
|---------|-------|---------|
| `maxit` / `maxgen` | `maxgen` | Maximum number of generations |
| `popsize` | `n.Cores` | Model runs per generation |
| `nCores` | `n.Cores` | Parallel workers; equal to `popsize` for full parallelism |
| `REPORT` | 1 | Save a restart every generation |
| `trace` | 3 | Report global and per-target fitness |

## 5. Run the calibration

`run_calibration()` starts a cluster with `n.Cores` workers, loads the
packages and objects each worker needs, and runs the AHR-ES (Adaptive
Hierarchical Recombination Evolution Strategy) optimiser, which is well suited
to the noisy, expensive fitness evaluations of ecosystem models.  Parameters
are estimated in the phases given by `parphase`.

```{r run-calibration}

results <- atlantiscalibration::run_calibration(calibration)
```

**Note:** For parallel calibration to work, the `atlantiscalibration` package must be
installed in the system library library(atlantiscalibratio)

If the calibration is interrupted, running it again with the same
`restart.file` continues from the last saved generation.

## 6. Inspect the results

The results are saved by calibrar in `<restart.file>.results`.
`compare_outputs()` compares the initial and optimised factors, and plots the
fitness of each target for the best solution of each generation:

```{r compare-outputs}
comparison <- compare_outputs(
  results_file = "/home/atlantis/Atlantis_Calibration/restart_file.results",
  forcing      = calibration$forcing
)

comparison$param_comparison  # factor_new: factor applied to the original parameter value
comparison$plot_changes
```

The trace of the optimisation has the global fitness
(`results$trace$value`), the fitness of each target (`results$trace$fitness`)
and the parameters (`results$trace$par`) of the best solution of each
generation:

```{r trace}
results <- readRDS("/home/atlantis/Atlantis_Calibration/restart_file.results")

matplot(results$trace$par, type = "l", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Generation", ylab = "Parameter (log factor)")
```

The calibrated parameter values are the original values multiplied by
`exp(results$par)`.  To create the calibrated parameter files, run
`run_model()` once with `results$par` in a copy of the model configuration.
